messages:
tess: Quick UX sync — I'm redesigning the compact capacity card for pools where min==max. Two open questions: microcopy for the primary CTA and how the inline confirm should behave for keyboard/screen-reader users.

maria: Thanks. From testing, people read the badge then the CTA. The badge should be explicit: 'Capacity locked' not 'Fixed capacity'. Also the subcopy must state who locked it if applicable (policy vs user).

aj: For CTAs, let's standardize: primary = 'Enable autoscaling', secondary = 'Edit min/max'. We ran into confusion when different screens said 'Enable burst' or 'Allow autoscale'. Keep it consistent across hosted/dedicated.

priya: Engineering note: use pool.supportsBurst and pool.lockedBy fields. If supportsBurst=false, show primary button but disabled with an accessible reason. Prefer visible but aria-disabled + aria-describedby rather than hiding it.

sam: Accessibility details: when aria-disabled is used, add a visible tooltip that is keyboard-focusable. Tooltip must be reachable via tab and closable with Esc. Also add a hidden sr-only string summarizing the card state for screen readers: e.g. 'Capacity locked. Autoscaling disabled.'

tess: Good. On the inline confirm: product prefers inline confirm (small bar) to avoid modal interruption. But it must behave like a dialog for a11y: role="dialog", focus trap while open, and an aria-live announcement when it appears: 'Inline confirmation: enabling autoscaling for pool X'.

maria: Copy for confirm: header 'Enable autoscaling?', body 'This will allow the pool to vary between {min} and {max}. Est. cost change: {value}.' Buttons: 'Confirm' (primary) / 'Cancel' (link). Keep text concise.

aj: Also add a tiny 'Why?' link that expands a short explanation about guardrails and fallback policies. Keep that link keyboard-accessible and ensure it doesn't steal focus away from the confirm.

priya: Implementation plan: reuse InlineConfirm component, which already sets role=dialog + focus trap. We'll add an aria-live region that announces details when opened and provide an escape handler to cancel. For disabled primary button add: aria-disabled="true" aria-describedby="why-disabled" and a tabbable tooltip with id="why-disabled" that reads 'Burst not supported on this pool'.

sam: Visual a11y: badge color needs to meet 4.5:1 in both light/dark at 14px. If color alone can't, add an icon and explicit text. Also ensure the cost delta line uses semantic text (no background-only color meaning).

ux-bot: Preview available: https://preview.redwood.design/branch/compact-confirm-a11y — includes keyboard walkthrough and sr-only examples.

tess: Action items: maria to update Figma strings (Enable autoscaling, Edit min/max, Capacity locked, Est. cost), aj to confirm wording parity across environments, priya to wire supportsBurst + lockedBy and reuse InlineConfirm, sam to add accessibility QA checks. I'll update the ticket with acceptance criteria (contrast, focus trap, tooltip tabindex, sr announcement). Thanks!
